properties.name: SHA-256
properties.note: Collision resistance 128 bits; reference point of NIST PQ category 2.

properties.name: SHA-384
properties.note: Only implicit: PRF hash of the TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 cipher suite (S24).

properties.name: SHA-512
properties.note: Category >= 4 (SHA-384 collision is the highest hash-based NIST reference point).

properties.name: MD5
properties.note: classicalSecurityLevel reflects the ~2^18 practical collision attack.

properties.name: SHA-1
properties.nistStatus: Disallowed for signature generation (SP 800-131A r2); NIST retires SHA-1 by 2030-12-31

properties.name: SHAKE128
properties.note: Used with a 256-bit output (min(d/2,128) = 128-bit collision resistance).

properties.name: HMAC-SHA256
properties.nistStatus: Approved (key >= 112 bits required; this corpus uses a 24-bit test key)
properties.note: Algorithm-level strength assumes a >=256-bit key; see m.hmac-key for the actual key.

properties.name: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256
properties.nistStatus: Approved (SP 800-132); 80,000 iterations is below the OWASP 2023 figure of 600,000
properties.note: Strength is bounded by password entropy, so no fixed security level is assigned.

properties.name: Argon2id
properties.nistStatus: Not NIST-approved (OWASP first choice for password storage)
properties.note: No standard OID is assigned. Internally uses BLAKE2b.

properties.name: bcrypt
properties.note: Eksblowfish-based password hash; passwords truncated at 72 bytes.

properties.name: AES-256-GCM
properties.note: 128-bit tag, 96-bit IV. Hard-coded key/IV in S11 are a published test vector.

properties.name: AES-256-CBC-PKCS7
properties.nistStatus: Approved mode; unauthenticated (padding-oracle risk without a MAC)

properties.name: AES-128-ECB-PKCS7
properties.nistStatus: Approved block cipher, but ECB leaks plaintext block equality - flag as weak mode

properties.name: AES-256-CTR
properties.note: No NIST OID is registered for AES-CTR.

properties.name: 3DES-CBC-PKCS7 (3-key TDEA)
properties.nistStatus: Disallowed for encryption after 2023-12-31 (SP 800-131A r2); decryption legacy-use only

properties.name: RSA-3072 key pair
properties.quantum: Broken by Shor's algorithm on a CRQC
properties.note: The same key pair is used for encryption (OAEP) and two signature schemes - a key-separation finding (SP 800-57 Pt 1 section 5.2).

properties.name: RSAES-OAEP-SHA256 (RSA-3072)
properties.quantum: Broken by Shor's algorithm on a CRQC
properties.note: Label hash SHA-256 and MGF1 hash SHA-256, empty label.

properties.name: RSASSA-PSS-SHA256 (RSA-3072)
properties.quantum: Broken by Shor's algorithm on a CRQC
properties.note: CycloneDX has no 'pss' padding value, so padding='other'. Salt length 32, trailer 0xBC.

properties.quantum: Broken by Shor's algorithm on a CRQC

notes.securerandom-default: On Linux, new SecureRandom() resolves to NativePRNG (SUN provider).
notes.key-label: Key-algorithm label inside a key spec; informational for HMAC keys.
notes.computed: Parameter is a constant expression, not a literal (evaluates to 16384).
notes.keysize-from-key: Key size is not named in code; it follows from the length of the key bytes (data-flow dependent).
notes.keygen-default-random: Key generator draws from the provider's default SecureRandom (implicit CSPRNG).
notes.aes-keygen-label: Mode-agnostic 'AES' key generator; the mode is only visible in the later transformation string.
notes.pkcs5-is-pkcs7: JCA name 'PKCS5Padding' denotes PKCS#7 padding for 16-byte blocks; normalise to pkcs7.
notes.desede-default-size: Key size is implicit: SunJCE's DESede KeyGenerator defaults to 168 bits (3-key TDEA).
notes.oaep-explicit: OAEP parameters are explicit; the bare transformation 'RSA/ECB/OAEPWithSHA-256AndMGF1Padding' would make SunJCE use SHA-1 for MGF1.
notes.ec-keygen-label: Generic 'EC' generator; the curve comes from a separate parameter spec.
notes.curve-alias: Curve alias; normalise to P-256 (secp256r1 = prime256v1 = P-256).
notes.seed-ctor: Key pair is derived deterministically from the hard-coded 32-byte seed.
notes.polymorphic-site: One call site serves two assets depending on the caller; recorded once per asset (context-sensitive).
notes.interprocedural: Algorithm literal reaches the API through a helper-method parameter (inter-procedural constant).
notes.kem-family-name: KEM API takes the family name; the parameter set comes from the key (ML-KEM-768).
notes.serial: CSPRNG output used for the certificate serial number (not key material).
notes.tls-context-name: SSLContext protocol name; enabled versions are set separately via SSLParameters.
notes.default-managers: null arguments select the default key/trust managers and SecureRandom.

runtimeNotes.note: new SecureRandom() and every KeyGenerator/KeyPairGenerator/Signature without an explicit random use the default SecureRandom; on Linux that is NativePRNG (SUN), backed by /dev/urandom.
'SHA256withRSA' and 'SHA256withECDSA' each name a hash and a scheme in one token.
JDK ML-DSA signing is hedged with an empty context by default.
SSLContext.init(null, null, null) uses the default trust store and SecureRandom. Named groups are the JDK 25 defaults (see Provider resolution); none is post-quantum.
